title: SqlAlchemy aiosqlite wrapper doesn't close the aiosqlite connection object (hanging thread)
body:
### Describe the bug

The aiosqlite dialect/wrapper never calls/awaits the underlying connection's `.close()` method, instead depending on having set [`connection.daemon = True`](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/7194b5ba3de050815ea20aafb80d262b6fcd1d07/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/sqlite/aiosqlite.py#L226) at connection time with the expectation that aiosqlite's thread will simply exit whenever the program using sqlalchemy exits. 

This a) potentially produces multiple stale threads if the user creates multiple connections via sqlalchemy, and b) leaves the aiosqlite/sqlite connection in an unknown state when the thread is unceremoniously killed at program exit time. More importantly, with aiosqlite v0.22.0, the connection class is no longer a thread, meaning `connection.daemon = True` does nothing, and this results in the aiosqlite connection hanging the program while it waits for its connection to be closed (https://github.com/omnilib/aiosqlite/issues/369).

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

main

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

aiosqlite 0.22.0

### Database Vendor and Major Version

sqlite

### Python Version

3.14

### Operating system

macOS

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine

async def main():
    engine = create_async_engine("sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:")
    print("connecting")
    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        print("connected")

    print("done")


asyncio.run(main())
```
